senses.definition: A knapsack, sometimes mounted on a light frame, but always supported by straps, worn on a person’s back for the purpose of carrying things, especially when hiking, or on a student's back when carrying books.

quotes.text: Rachel discovered that she could also keep things in her backpack that were important to her, nobody would know about them because they would be hidden. These important things included a small round rock that she had found […]

quotes.text: Many seats carry reservation labels, while the luggage racks are festooned with backpacks and suitcases.
quotes.reference: 2022 November 30, Paul Bigland, “Destination Oban: a Sunday in Scotland”, in RAIL, number 971, page 77:

senses.definition: A similarly placed item containing a parachute or other life-support equipment.
(intransitive) To hike and camp overnight in backcountry with one's gear carried in a backpack.
examples: I spent a month backpacking in the Rockies.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To engage in low-cost, generally urban, travel with minimal luggage and frugal accommodation.
(transitive, rare) To place or carry (an item or items) in a backpack.

quotes.text: I planned to go to jungle today and backpacked my things which contained ^([sic]) food and a note book.
